description: The context-fed reference generation fixture: gen schema generates the committed processing/bind/context-fed-reference schema, whose ShelfRef and PlacedRef fields take their value from a String-typed context slot when the book writes none, twice into two scratch trees the harness requires byte-identical; the generated crate compiles inside a scratch workspace materialized from this scenario's committed template, and the compiled processor collects the committed data document as a reading linked under complete scope through its own typed reader. Before the binder decoded context-fed values through the field's type, the typed handlers rejected every such book as KDLITH-GEN003 and dropped it; now both books read, the context-fed shelf and the one-element tags list resolve to the fiction shelf, the explicit shelf property still wins on the second book, and the contextual placed reference carries the room it was bound under (Ref::context) and resolves to that room's spot, with no diagnostic. The same exercise then pins the KDL writer the generated crate re-exports: it renders a document whose names and strings carry quotes, backslashes, newlines, tabs, a bidi control, a non-breaking space, an empty string, identifier values written bare or quoted as their spelling requires, and names that read as numbers, keywords, or carry a space, and reads the text back with kdlith-parse; the rendered text, every parser event over it, and is_bare_string's answers are pinned byte for byte, so a writer that loses a character or writes text the parser reads differently fails

stdout-contains:
schema ok digest=362829ae25d7ccd8
read failed=false books=2 diagnostics=0
book Dune shelf=fiction->fiction tags=[fiction->fiction] placed=fiction context=attic -> attic.fiction
book Odes shelf=poetry->poetry tags=[fiction->fiction] placed=fiction context=attic -> attic.fiction

"123" "true"="x=y" "has space"="#z"

}

end

end

end
